parts.label: Understand
parts.title: Draw the shared request path
parts.body:
An enterprise AI platform should make common controls usable across products while leaving each business team responsible for its workflow. Trace one request from authenticated user through application, policy check, retrieval or tools, model route, response validation, and audit record. Draw trust boundaries: where personal or confidential information enters, which service can call a model provider, and where an answer is stored or shown. A diagram with named owners is more useful to a C-suite decision than a box labeled 'AI platform.'

Shared services often include identity, secrets, approved model routes, retrieval connectors, evaluation, telemetry, policy configuration, and cost accounting. These are capabilities, not a requirement to move all data into one store. A team building a customer service assistant should still own its source content, user interaction, escalation, outcome metrics, and incident response. Platform owners can provide paved paths and evidence, while security and privacy owners set their requirements.

Google Cloud's enterprise GenAI blueprint describes identity, networking, logging, monitoring, deployment, and policy checks as foundation capabilities. The diagram is an example of one vendor's implementation; the same questions apply to an on-premises or multivendor design. Ask which components are already reliable, which must be built, and where provider-specific integration is worth the lock-in. Put data residency, transfer, and retention decisions at each boundary rather than assuming a cloud region settles them.

example.title: An integrated request path
example.body: An Ontario employee signs in to the HR application (identity team). The application passes role and region to a policy service; an HR-owned index retrieves only current Ontario documents the employee may read (HR and data owners). The gateway strips unnecessary identifiers and sends limited passages to an approved model route (platform team), crossing a provider trust boundary governed by security and privacy review. The application checks that citations resolve to authorized versions before showing an answer (HR product team). A minimal audit event records configuration and source versions under an approved retention rule (platform and privacy owners). If authorization, retrieval, or validation fails, the application gives a manual HR contact and alerts the operator. The release owner can disable this route at the gateway; HR maintains the manual service.

exercise.title: Draw and defend the path
exercise.body: Sketch the request path for one use case. Mark identity checks, data stores, model boundary, secret holder, output destination, logs, human fallback, and an emergency stop. Assign an owner to each boundary and explain it to a CISO in two minutes.

sources: Google Cloud: enterprise GenAI and MLOps blueprint
European Commission: data protection by design and default

parts.label: Practice
parts.title: Choose what to centralize
parts.body:
Centralize a capability when repeated local implementations create risk or waste and a shared service can support different workflows. Approved model access, secrets, request metadata, access-policy integration, evaluation tooling, and cost telemetry often qualify. Keep domain rules, customer journey, source ownership, and benefit measurement close to the business. If the platform team becomes the approver of every prompt change, it can slow small experiments without improving control. Set interfaces and release conditions by risk instead.

Compare build, buy, and partner choices component by component. A vendor gateway may shorten time to launch but needs checks on identity integration, data handling, portability, observability, contractual rights, and price under real usage. Building your own retrieval stack gives more control but commits engineers to index updates, permission sync, evaluation, and on-call support. A hybrid can use a purchased model service behind an enterprise gateway and keep sensitive retrieval in a managed data boundary. Calculate total cost over a plausible load range, including the cost of switching providers.

Define service levels for platform functions that applications depend on. If the gateway fails, can the application queue a request, degrade to a manual path, or switch to an approved model? Who authorizes a new provider, handles a security incident, or updates the policy? The platform charter should specify those decision rights and chargeback or allocation method so a business sponsor sees the whole run cost.

example.title: Build-buy decision with exit cost
example.body: For a hypothetical HR pilot, a managed gateway costs $90,000 yearly at the expected load plus $30,000 integration, with built-in budget caps and a 60-day export path for logs and configurations. Building costs $220,000 in engineering and on-call time in year one, then $110,000 yearly, but permits custom routing. Both require the same regional permission tests and application evaluation. The team buys for the pilot, retains model routes and evaluation records in portable formats, caps spend per department, and rehearses switching a route. It will build only if projected volume or unmet controls reverse the two-year total-cost comparison. These numbers are illustrative, not vendor quotes.

exercise.title: Make a build-buy table
exercise.body: For gateway, retrieval, evaluation, and monitoring, compare build, buy, and partner on launch time, controls, run cost, skills, exit path, and owner. Choose one component to centralize and one to leave with a product team; explain the boundary.

sources: Google Cloud: enterprise GenAI and MLOps blueprint
NIST AI RMF Core: third-party risk and governance

parts.label: Operate
parts.title: Put evidence and controls in the path
parts.body:
A gateway can enforce approved routes, limits, and logging, but it cannot judge every answer's truth or business effect. Each application needs an evaluation set drawn from its actual work, including difficult cases and affected populations. Use shared evaluation tools so release teams can compare configurations and keep results, while domain experts define what a correct and useful answer means. Capture source version, prompt and model configuration, response status, cost, latency, and user correction signals as permitted by privacy rules.

Design policy checks near the action they protect. Identity must be checked before retrieval; authorization must cover a tool call that writes to a business system; an output destined for a customer may need different review from an internal draft. Define circuit breakers for spending spikes, provider outages, repeated unsafe outputs, and known data leaks. An emergency stop should state who can trigger it and what manual workflow remains.

Report platform health separately from product benefit. Gateway uptime, p95 latency, cost per request, and policy-check failures tell the platform team whether its service works. Resolution time, error rate, appeal volume, and adoption tell the business whether the use case works. If a model route changes, run application evaluations before exposing all traffic. NIST's Measure and Manage functions call for evaluation in context and responses to observed risk.

example.title: A release trace
example.body: A service assistant changes model provider. The platform confirms routing and spend limits; the product team checks representative answers and escalation behavior. A 5% canary monitors latency, cost, quality, and complaints before wider rollout. The percentage is illustrative.

exercise.title: Specify a release gate
exercise.body: For one application, list five signals split between platform health and business outcomes. Define a canary, rollback condition, owner, and manual fallback. Show where each signal is collected in your request diagram.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: Measure and Manage
Google Cloud: MLOps monitoring and deployment

parts.label: Apply
parts.title: Approve an architecture with conditions
parts.body:
An architecture review should ask what decision is being made: approve a limited pilot, authorize a provider, fund a shared service, or permit production scale. Present the request path, trust boundaries, major alternatives, expected load and cost range, failure modes, control owners, and remaining decisions. A diagram without the operating team, evaluation evidence, and incident route is incomplete.

For a regulated company, split the review by data class and region. EU personal data processing needs the applicable GDPR basis and design controls. In Canada, PIPEDA may apply to commercial activities, while provincial and sector laws can change the answer; accountability for processing by a third party still needs attention. An EU AI Act high-risk classification depends on intended use, such as certain employment or credit decisions, rather than merely using a foundation model. Legal and privacy teams establish obligations; the architecture shows how the chosen controls work.

Give executives an explicit tradeoff. A single global service may be cheaper to operate but complicate regional data and vendor requirements. Separate regional deployments may simplify some boundaries while increasing duplication and upgrade burden. Recommend a design with conditions and cost of compliance, then record who accepts residual operational risk. Revisit the decision when use, provider, or data category changes.

example.title: Approval from the architecture record
example.body: Approve the Ontario HR pilot on the managed gateway described above, capped at its expected annual spend and restricted to an HR-owned regional index. Identity and permission sync, source-citation validation, privacy review of the provider boundary, and an emergency gateway stop are release conditions. HR owns answers and the manual fallback; platform owns route limits, telemetry, and rollback. Reassess build versus buy after measured volume and a route-switch rehearsal; EU expansion requires a separate regional and privacy review.

exercise.title: Write the architecture decision
exercise.body: Prepare a one-page decision record with two design alternatives, trust boundaries, regional assumptions, total-cost categories, control owner, evaluation gate, fallback, and a date to reassess. State what further use would require a new review.

sources: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada: PIPEDA accountability
EU AI Act Service Desk: Annex III
